newsitem.title: NORWAY: Alliance ministers meet on Bosnia force.
newsitem.headline: Alliance ministers meet on Bosnia force.

text.p: NATO defence ministers met on Wednesday for talks on a new peace force for Bosnia, attempts to reform the alliance for post-Cold War tasks, and how to build a new relationship with Russia.

The 16 ministers opened their annual informal session in the Norwegian port city of Bergen with their first formal discussion of what to do in Bosnia when the mandate of the current 55,000-strong force expires in late-December.
The allies agree some force has to remain in 1997 to stop the country sliding back into war, but the issue is highly sensitive in the United States ahead of November's presidential elections.

The informal meeting will not take a final decision, but allow countries to give views on the size, exact composition, mandate, and length of stay of any follow-on force to the alliance's Implementation Force (IFOR).
The meeting will also discuss reform of the alliance's command structures to allow it to undertake more Bosnia-style peace missions and confirm itself as the continent's main security organisation.

On Thursday, they will move on to plans to extend the alliance next year to take in former enemies from former communist eastern Europe and its often-stormy relations with Russia which remains opposed to the scheme.
